source.title: 100-epoch ImageNet Training with AlexNet in 24 Minutes
source.authors: Yang You; Zhao Zhang; Cho-Jui Hsieh; J. Demmel; K. Keutzer

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether larger batches worsen held-out image-classification accuracy at a fixed epoch count, using ImageNet AlexNet and ResNet-50 results with different batch sizes and training recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own ImageNet test-accuracy results for batch-size comparisons. It also discusses prior-work results and shows figures; cited prior-work results are not extracted as rows. Communication and runtime measurements do not bear on a claim version.
record.test_reason: Own fixed-epoch ImageNet experiments compare small and large batches under linear scaling, warmup and LARS, directly testing V5's batch penalty and recipe-dependent recovery. This study is not an original source listed for V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that LARS enables batch-32K synchronous training to scale across many processors while retaining approximately baseline ImageNet accuracy: 100-epoch AlexNet in 11 minutes and 90-epoch ResNet-50 in 20 minutes. They also examine augmentation. This conclusion does not extend to arbitrary batch sizes: Table 10 shows accuracy losses at 64K.
record.recipe_differences: ImageNet training with synchronous SGD scaled using LARS and warmup; it does not test random-label memorization or the generalization-measure interventions named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size, use of data augmentation, LARS versus linear scaling with warmup, and—in AlexNet at batch size 32K—changing local response normalization to batch normalization.
record.code_released: Our code is available upon request.
record.problems: The comparisons vary hardware and, in some settings, data augmentation or model normalization alongside batch size. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper notes that its augmented ResNet-50 baseline is below Facebook's reported result and that it could not reproduce a full match.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 includes several other learning-rate and warmup combinations for AlexNet at batch size 4096; not extracted beyond the reported 0.531 result and the 0.001 result because those cover the stated selected outcome and a distinctly worse reported setting. Table 9's 64-epoch ResNet-50 result is omitted because it does not hold the epoch budget fixed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Adam or related adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning; LARS alone does not supply this comparison.
Language models, recovery through longer training, and generality beyond AlexNet and ResNet-50 on ImageNet.
Dropout interventions or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.

missing.what: Own ResNet-50 results at batch 65536: 70.0% without augmentation versus 73.0% at batch 256, and 73.2% with weak augmentation versus 75.3%. These 90-epoch results reveal a remaining batch-size limit under LARS.
Own unaugmented ResNet-50 result at batch 16384: 72.7% versus the 73.0% batch-256 baseline after 90 epochs.

ResNet-50 comparison of linear scaling plus warmup against LARS plus warmup at batches 16K and 32K. The text reports approximately 68% and 56% without LARS versus a target near 73%; extract the plotted LARS endpoints and confirm the epoch budgets.
missing.locator: Scaling up Batch Size; Figure 4 and caption

missing.what: Additional own AlexNet peak accuracies: batch 512 gives 58.8% on DGX-1 and batch 32768 gives 58.6% on 1024 CPUs after 100 epochs. Preserve the distinction between these peak values and Table 7's reported test accuracies.

record.verdict_notes: States marked observed for adapted recipes refer to V5's explicit recovery clause. Small residual penalties are partial recovery, not evidence that adaptation never helps. Hardware, normalization and augmentation differ across some comparisons; no uncertainty estimates are supplied. The blanket introductory statement that no results use augmentation conflicts with the later explicitly augmented results; use the table-specific conditions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons.
Language models; broad batch-size thresholds across workloads; comparisons with smaller-batch recipes beyond the ImageNet settings tested.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
